--- title: "Data at scale" description: "Lazy frames and streams of batches, threads, and compressed data on disk." order: 4 jupyter: python3 --- Everything in the previous articles works on rows that do not fit in memory. The passes read the rows once (or twice, for two-pass effects), in batches, and keep only the compressed rows. ::: {#9a971fcd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import polars as pl import ume from ume.testing import simulate_accounts folder = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) simulate_accounts(50_000, seed=7).sample(fraction=1.0, shuffle=True, seed=1).write_parquet(folder / "rows.parquet") ``` ::: ## A lazy frame `annotate` accepts a polars `LazyFrame`. The reference points and levels are resolved with one lazy aggregation, the rows are sorted by cluster lazily, and the passes stream them in batches: ::: {#7cadd123 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} exp = ume.annotate( pl.scan_parquet(folder / "rows.parquet"), cluster="account", instrument="Z", treatment="T", cohort="day", covariates=ume.covariates("x1", "x2", kids=0, device=ume.categorical(reference="tv")), ).metrics(ume.mean("y", name="hours"), ume.ratio("N", "D", name="rebuffers_per_play")) exp ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html} naive plan: (run LazyFrame.explain(optimized=True) to see the optimized plan)

``` ::: ::: ## A stream of batches For any other source, declare the design with every reference point and level fixed, and pass an iterable of frames grouped by cluster. Two-pass methods need to read the rows twice, so give them a function that returns the batches: ::: {#8ec29119 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} design = ume.design( cluster="account", instrument="Z", treatment="T", cohort="day", covariates=ume.covariates(x1=2.0, x2=2.0, kids=0, device=ume.categorical(reference="tv", levels=["tv", "mobile", "web"])), metrics=[ume.mean("y", name="hours"), ume.ratio("N", "D", name="rebuffers_per_play")], ) def batches(): rows = pl.read_parquet(folder / "rows.parquet").sort("account") for lo in range(0, len(rows), 25_000): yield rows[lo : lo + 25_000] ume.compress(batches(), design).fit().effects() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## The exact bootstrap over shards Exact-bootstrap weights depend only on (seed, cluster, draw), so shards processed separately produce sums that add. Merge them, then fit every draw once, because a draw's propensities need the whole cohort: ::: {#224835fa .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = pl.read_parquet(folder / "rows.parquet") parts = [ume.bootstrap_sums(rows.filter(pl.col("account") % 3 == k), design, B=500, seed=1) for k in range(3)] (parts[0] + parts[1] + parts[2]).draws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The multinomial (classical) bootstrap cannot be split: its counts are coupled across all clusters. ## Threads Passes and draw fits run on `ume.get_threads()` workers, by default `min(4, cores)`. Each cluster goes to one worker, by a hash of its key, and the workers' compressed rows add at the end, the same way shards do. The results do not depend on the number of threads beyond the order of floating-point additions: ::: {#8f982564 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} ume.get_threads() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: ## Compressed data on disk A compressed dataset saves to a single file, with its design, layout and strata, and loads back exactly. Shards saved on different machines merge with `+`: ::: {#1993cad7 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} for k in range(3): shard = ume.compress(pl.read_parquet(folder / "rows.parquet").filter(pl.col("account") % 3 == k), design) shard.save(folder / f"shard{k}.npz") merged = sum((ume.load(folder / f"shard{k}.npz") for k in range(1, 3)), ume.load(folder / "shard0.npz")) merged ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
